title: GCD: GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling across Heterogeneous GCMs
claim: Supervised and vanilla posterior-sampling approaches have limitations; our method adds conditioning, filtered guidance and distillation to run inference in far fewer steps.
layout: 3 rows by 2 columns, training left and inference right, dashed row dividers
description: A grid comparing three downscaling paradigms across two columns, Training Stage on the left and Inference Stage on the right. Row (a) is a supervised model: a coarse ERA5 field X' gets noise added and a network f_theta maps it to X. At inference, a GCM field Y gets noise added and goes through f_theta by direct transfer to produce the downscaled output. Row (b) is vanilla DPS: X is noised to Gaussian noise N and denoised with DDPM using p_theta(X). At inference, GD guidance from Y steers the DDPM chain. Row (c) is the proposed GCD method: the same pipeline, plus a condition C that constrains p_theta(X|C), which is distilled into p_phi(X|C). At inference, a filtered Y gives GD or CG guidance and a DDIM sampler. New components are drawn in orange, and the row label reads 1000 steps / 6 steps. Circles are variables and rounded boxes are models. Blue boxes, green Y nodes and orange distilled parts carry the color coding.
caption: Schematic comparison of different downscaling paradigms during training and inference.
abstract: Climate downscaling of General Circulation Models (GCMs) is an ill-posed inverse problem, as GCM outputs and reanalysis fields arise from different dynamical systems and lack fine-scale temporal pairing. Supervised methods thus rely on synthetic degradations or model-specific adaptation, limiting generalization across heterogeneous GCMs. Zero-shot diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) avoids paired supervision by combining a high-resolution climate prior with inference-time constraints from coarse GCM inputs, but faces consistency and efficiency challenges. We propose GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling (GCD), which addresses these challenges with geographic conditioning, spectrally filtered measurement guidance, and distillation-accelerated Conjugate Gradient guidance. GCD reduces inference from 1,000 diffusion steps to 6 while maintaining consistency with the coarse GCM inputs. Across five heterogeneous GCMs, GCD achieves competitive 99th-percentile extreme-event accuracy and reconstructs plausible high-frequency tropical cyclone structures without model-specific retraining. Github: https://github.com/shawnvonbohr/GCD-Climate-Downscaling.git
